newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Union Re says premiums ease on pressures.
newsitem.headline: Union Re says premiums ease on pressures.

text.p: Union Reinsurance Co., part of Swiss Reinsurance Co., said its premium volume declined in 1996 because it had continued its profit-oriented underwriting policy despite considerable pressure on rates.

Although Union Re's 1996 gross premiums rose 11.6 percent to 1.43 billion Swiss francs, the company said in a statement that considering the weakness of the Swiss franc and much earlier closing of accounts, the premium volume "actually declined slightly compared with the previous year."

Union Re said the reasons for this decline was that competition within the industry had sharpened following several years of positive insurance and reinsurance results and the absence of major catastrophe losses.
"Pressure on rates was considerable, and they often fell below the level required to meet our goals for return on equity," Union Re said, adding:
"In this difficult situation, Union Re continue its profitability-oriented underwriting policy, hence the reduction in premium volume."

The company also said that taxes rose in 1996, partially due to higher profit in the previous year but also because provisions were posted, for the first time, in the amount of the estimated taxes on current profit.
